problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+4t{y}^{′}+2y={e}^{t},\,t>0
$$

has the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(t)=\frac{A}{t}+\frac{B}{{t}^{2}}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(t)$ to this equation. 

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result:* 

$$
\int t{e}^{t}\text{d}t=(t-1){e}^{t}+C
$$

feedback.problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-x{y}^{′}-3y={x}^{4}{e}^{x},\,x>0
$$

has the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(x)=\frac{A}{x}+B{x}^{3}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation. 

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result:* 

$$
\int {x}^{4}{e}^{x}\text{d}x=({x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}-24x+24){e}^{x}+C
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the differential equation to the form

$$
{y}^{″}+P(x){y}^{′}+Q(x)y=f(x).
$$

So, we divide both sides of the given equation by ${x}^{2}.$ We get

$$
{y}^{″}-\frac{1}{x}{y}^{′}-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}y={x}^{2}{e}^{x}.
$$

We notice that the forcing term $f(x)={x}^{2}{e}^{x}.$ Additionally, we're given the fundamental solutions:

$$
{y}_{1}(x)=\frac{1}{x},\,{y}_{2}(x)={x}^{3}
$$

First, let's compute the Wronskian:

$$
\begin{aligned}W({y}_{1},{y}_{2}) & =|\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}^{′} & {y}_{2}^{′}\end{aligned}| \\  & ={y}_{1}{y}_{2}^{′}-{y}_{1}^{′}{y}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}({x}^{3})^{′}-{(\frac{1}{x})}^{′}{x}^{3} \\  & =3{x}^{2}(\frac{1}{x})-(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}){x}^{3} \\  & =3x+x \\  & =4x\ne 0\end{aligned}
$$

Since the Wronskian is not equal to zero, this confirms that the functions  ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)$ are independent. 

According to the method of variation of parameters, the particular solution of the differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}(x) & ={y}_{1}(x)u(x)+{y}_{2}(x)v(x),\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x) & =-\int \frac{f(x){y}_{2}(x)}{W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{4}\int {x}^{4}{e}^{x}\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{4}({x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}-24x+24){e}^{x}, \\ v(x) & =\int \frac{f(x){y}_{1}(x)}{W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\int {e}^{x}\text{d}x=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}(x) & ={y}_{1}(x)u(x)+{y}_{2}(x)v(x) \\  & =(\frac{1}{x})(-\frac{1}{4}({x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}-24x+24){e}^{x})+({x}^{3})(\frac{1}{4}{e}^{x}) \\  & =(-\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}+{x}^{2}-3x+6-\frac{6}{x}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}){e}^{x} \\  & =({x}^{2}-3x+6-\frac{6}{x}){e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
